newsitem.title: USA: Unisys on track for full year goals.
newsitem.headline: Unisys on track for full year goals.

text.p: Unisys Corp said that it is on track to achieve its financial goals for the rest of the year, after reporting second quarter earnings that surpassed Wall Street expectations.

Unisys reported a profit of $0.08 a share, after payment of preferred dividends, compared to a loss of $0.14 a share a year ago. According to First Call, the consensus estimate on Wall Street was for earnings of $0.05 a share.
In April, Unisys said it goal is to deliver year-over-year financial progress and full-year profitability in 1997.
"We are on track to achieve our financial goals for the year," said James Unruh, chairman and CEO, in a statement.

Unisys said that its revenues were up five percent to $1.59 billion, from $1.51 billion a year ago, its cash flow improved and its operating profit margin almost doubled from a year ago, to margins of 8.1 percent of revenue.
In particular, Unisys said its Computer Systems Group turned in another very good profit and revenue performance and its Information Services Group continues to make progress toward profits.
Unisys posted double-digit revenue growth in the U.S., versus the year-ago period. Despite the negative impact of currency translation, revenue from international markets was up slightly.

Unisys said revenues in its Computer Systems Group grew 10 percent versus a year ago, based on strong demand for its ClearPath enterprise servers. Gross profit margins were up five percentage points from year ago levels in computers.
Its Information Services Group is on target to achieve operating profitability on a run-rate basis by year-end 1997 and to return to profit margins of 21.3 percent.
This improvement helped the Information Services group narrow its operating loss to $17.8 million from $49.5 million in the first quarter of 1997.

Customer revenues in its Global Customer Services group increased 11 percent over the year-ago quarter, driven by continued strong growth in distributed computing support services. Gross profit margins were down from a year ago, due to the shift in the business mix away from proprietary maintenance to distributed computing services.
Operating profits for the group rose slightly.
Overall, worldwide orders were up slightly from a year ago.
